newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ML's CEPA 1997 warrantholders may get cash - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: ML's CEPA 1997 warrantholders may get cash - Merrill.

text.p: Merrill Lynch International and Co said on Monday the terms and conditions of its Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) 1997 covered warrant may be adjusted to allow for warrantholders to receive cash.
The warrants, which were last traded on October 7 and closed the day at HK$0.475, resumed trading on Monday. The warrant gained only HK$0.005 to trade at HK$0.48 in the morning session.
In a notice issued by the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong, Merrill Lynch said under the terms of the issue, the conditions of the warrants may be adjusted.
Adjustments can be made no later than the business day preceding the consummation of such a merger and delisting, it said.
The amendments would allow for holders of warrants exercised after such business day to be entitled to receive a cash payment in lieu of shares, the notice said.

CEPA parent Hopewell Holdings Ltd announced last Thursday that it was selling 80 percent of its holding in CEPA to Southern Co of the U.S. in a move which would most likely lead to the privatisation and delisting of CEPA.
A decision by CEPA shareholders on the Southern takeover plan and delisting of CEPA was likely by the end of the year, the Hopewell announcement said.
If the Southern offer is accepted and the privatisation scheme becomes effecitve, it is expected that the warrants will be withdrawn from listing, the Merrill Lynch notice said.
